summary.headline: PDS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to ₹3,444 crores and PAT rose 43% to ₹29 crores, with net debt cut 73% to ₹29 crores.
summary.overview: PDS grew GMV 11% to ₹5,146 crores and revenue 15% to ₹3,444 crores, led by North America sales up 48%. EBITDA rose 90% to ₹96 crores, with margin up 111 bps to 2.8%, and PAT grew 43% to ₹29 crores. Order book rose 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crores, and net working capital fell to 1 day. Management framed the year as a shift from building the platform to scaling it, though it declined to raise guidance until mid-year.

financial_highlights.change: down 73% from ₹105 crores in Q4 FY26
vs ₹40 crores in Q1 FY26, which included ~₹22 crores FX gain

segments.name: Sourcing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹3,272 crores, up 16% YoY; EBIT ₹58 crores at 1.8% margin.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹227 crores, up 4% YoY; EBIT ₹15 crores at 6.5% margin, mainly from value-retail customers. Busana Apparel Group partnership aims to move mix toward fashion customers.

segments.name: New verticals
segments.commentary: Investment ₹37 crores in Q1, down 8% YoY from ₹41 crores; brand management investment down 38%, design-led sourcing down 5%. North America investment rising with GSCL scale-up.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Americas revenue up 48% YoY; Europe revenue up 21%. Ted Baker losses were about $2 million PBT in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management asked analysts to focus on Q2 repeating the Q1 trend and to revisit guidance after mid-year; it did not give a formal FY27 number.
Interest cost expected to stay flat to lower in USD terms; rupee cost is higher. Average USD borrowing cost about 7-8%.
New verticals P&L impact for the full year expected to be in line with prior internal expectations, with improvement each quarter.
Ted Baker losses for FY27 expected not to exceed $2-3 million.
Working capital to remain in low single-digit days, possibly 0-1 days in some quarters.
Investment in PDS Ventures capped at under ₹10 crores a year (about $1-1.5 million).
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose 21% to ₹36 crores, reflecting the Knit Gallery acquisition and capitalisation of the UK office property.

Asset-light sourcing model used to add third-party factories; management said it can onboard 4-5 third-party factories within about 6 months for a ~$100 million Marks & Spencer opportunity, versus $50-60 million of capex if built in-house.
Egypt being explored as a base with duty-free access to the US.
Upgrade of SAP to S/4HANA under way; AI and digital investment across sourcing, pricing, supply management and operations.
Sourcing-as-a-service GMV under execution was about ₹1,700 crores in Q1, excluding newly signed contracts.
demand_pricing: Order book up 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crores; management says new mandates represent annual business potential of about US$330 million over 3-4 year contracts.
Largest French apparel retailer signed on a sourcing-as-a-service contract with option value of $300-400 million GMV over next 2 years.
US accounts including Walmart, Coles, Fashion Nova, TJ Maxx, PVH and American Eagle onboarded; 70-80% of key US accounts opened.
Europe: Mango (Spain) scaling, CCC (Poland) onboarded; Gerry Weber bankruptcy replaced by new German accounts.
Sourcing-as-a-service economics: GMV to revenue about 2.5%, revenue to PBT about 25%, per management extrapolation.
Matalan account fell from about $140 million to $70 million, and Gerry Weber was lost; management says there was no bad debt from either.

qa_highlights.question: Given order book growth of 23% and Q1 revenue growth of 15%, should growth be higher than the mid-single-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the team will stay focused on Q2 repeating the trend and will revisit guidance after mid-year.

qa_highlights.question: Is new-vertical investment on track toward about ₹80 crores, and what about North America losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 new-vertical investment was ₹37 crores and that full-year P&L impact should be in line with expectations, with more profitability in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will finance costs keep rising with factoring as revenue grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said interest cost is flat in USD terms, and rupee cost is up. Early payment discounts are being used to fund supplier discounts, and the company will disclose EPD against interest cost from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1-day working capital structural or cyclical?
qa_highlights.answer: Sadik Sunasara said it reflects a higher share of factorable receivables, and the target is low single-digit days, possibly 0-1 in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Where does AI add value: cost savings or revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Pallak Seth cited a China subsidiary whose turnover doubled from $60 million to $120 million with 60 staff using low-cost AI tools; he said the benefit is mainly productivity for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 555 strategy still achievable given setbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said the 12-18 months were spent fixing the Gerry Weber and Matalan impact and that growth is back in Q1 and in the order book; management will focus on quarterly EBITDA-margin improvement rather than a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ted Baker loss and the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 Ted Baker losses were about $2 million PBT, and FY27 losses are expected not to exceed $2-3 million; the IPR owner Authentic Brands Group is being kept informed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business is brand management, and what is it worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Jain said New Lobster/Ted Baker revenue is about ₹100 crores, other licensed brands about ₹350 crores a year (about ₹90 crores a quarter), and brand management will be scaled slowly over the next 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Bangladesh concentration (over 50% of sourcing) likely to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect absolute Bangladesh volumes to fall, but expects India's and other countries' share to rise through Knit Gallery and Egypt.

risks_watch: Growth quality: management declined to raise guidance and asked for another quarter of proof before revisiting it.
Finance cost: flat in USD terms only if early payment discount use continues; disclosure of EPD vs interest cost promised from Q2.
Ted Baker/New Lobster: about $2 million Q1 loss; resolution with Authentic Brands Group pending; no formal resolution yet.
New verticals: Ted Baker has moved out of the new-verticals line after about 3 years, which can change segment comparisons; GSCL investment rising in North America.
Other income fell to ₹9 crores from ₹40 crores in Q1 FY26, which included a ~₹22 crores FX gain; this will drag on reported PBT.
Concentration: over 50% of sourcing from Bangladesh, and geopolitical risk per management.
Execution: the US$330 million mandates and the French sourcing-as-a-service contract (option $300-400 million GMV) need to convert to revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and balance sheet, with specific numbers. Cautious on forward guidance, deferring any guidance revision to mid-year. Evasive on some detail: the call dropped during Pallak Seth's answers on AI and brand-management economics, and the finance-cost answer was given at length without a hard number.
key_quotes: We are gradually now happy to see this translating into numbers.
So my request and specific response to your question is that let's stay focused on one more healthy quarter and maybe post the mid of the year, we can revisit any of the guidance or anything.
So, therefore, you know, the GMV that I have, 2.5% of that comes to revenue and whatever revenue I have, 25% of that comes to PBT.

adds.what: 4-5 third-party factories onboarded via asset-light sourcing for ~$100M Marks & Spencer opportunity
Egypt explored as base with duty-free US access

growth.why: No formal FY27 revenue number; management declined to raise guidance until mid-year, but Q1 revenue rose 15% and order book rose 23% to ₹6,095 cr, with new mandates of ~US$330M annual potential and partial backing via third-party factory onboarding (4-5 factories in ~6 months).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 111 bps to 2.8% (vs 1.7%) and gross margin up 63 bps to 20%, with new verticals losses to narrow each quarter and management targeting quarterly EBITDA-margin improvement, though it gave no hard margin number.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new owned plant is planned; growth comes via asset-light third-party factories (4-5 onboarded in about 6 months for a ~$100M M&S opportunity vs $50-60M capex in-house), and Egypt is only being explored.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book up 23% YoY to ₹6,095 crores, GMV up 11% to ₹5,146 crores, and new mandates worth about US$330M annual potential over 3-4 years, although management asked to see Q2 repeat the Q1 trend before revising guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is capped at under ₹10 crores a year for PDS Ventures and the asset-light model avoids $50-60M in-house factory capex, so no major capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to raise guidance and deferred any revision to mid-year, but Q1 revenue grew 15% and the order book grew 23%, so an upgrade is possible if Q2 repeats the Q1 trend.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Matalan account fell from about $140M to $70M and Gerry Weber was lost, and Ted Baker losses (about $2M in Q1, FY27 capped at $2-3M) and Bangladesh concentration above 50% of sourcing remain risks.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Brand management is to be scaled slowly over the next 2-3 quarters on about ₹90 crores a quarter of licensed-brand revenue, and the AI and digital upgrade (SAP S/4HANA) is under way, but no specific new product or brand launch was named.

rows.label: Net working capital at 1 day, low single-digit target
rows.why: NWC fell from 4 days in March 2026 to 1 day, with the target of low single-digit days (possibly 0-1 in some quarters) because of a higher share of factorable receivables; cash from operations was ₹151 crores in Q1.

rows.label: Net debt cut to ₹29 crores
rows.why: Net debt fell 73% from ₹105 crores in Q4 FY26 to ₹29 crores, and interest cost is guided flat to lower in USD terms (USD borrowing about 7-8%), though rupee cost is higher and depends on continued early-payment-discount use.

rows.label: French sourcing-as-a-service contract
rows.why: The largest French apparel retailer signed a contract with option value of $300-400M GMV over 2 years, but it is conditional on the options being exercised and not yet converted to revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, order book and balance sheet but cautious on guidance, deferring any revision to mid-year; analysts pushed on why growth was not raised, finance cost trajectory, and working capital sustainability, and the call dropped during answers on AI and brand economics.
